objective: Qualify a bounded fake-target deployment state machine with explicit source/authorization binding, fencing, persist-before-dispatch, uncertain outcome reconciliation, migration/health faults, and recovery. No live deployment.
nonGoals: No production or staging deployment, remote network calls, external secrets or target writes
No automatic promotion of SF-14 self-supplied release pin into authenticated authorization
No claim that synthetic in-memory fencing proves distributed locking, disk durability or real adapter semantics
No CI workflow, branch protection or external project changes
decisions: Use pure fake-target simulation and independently checked state transitions; no adapter with live deployment authority.
Require persisted intent before fake dispatch and exact idempotency/fence correlation for eventual recovery; unknown outcomes cannot be replayed as fresh actions.
Fail closed on stale grant, wrong destination/source/artifact, mutation and health failure. Failure vs unknown vs compensated are separate states.

obligations.description: Reject expired/revoked or stale grant/epoch and conflicting concurrent owners before simulated dispatch; bind source, destination, artifact and grant identities.

Exercise injection matrix: concurrent admission, stale authorization, migration pre/post-dispatch failure, crash after dispatch, unknown outcome, health failure; require per-scenario expected trace/outcome.
On restart, reconcile unresolved dispatches against trusted fake-target receipts before any replay; prevent duplicate effects and distinguish unresolved, failed, compensated and recovered outcomes.
No live target invocation, credentials, network, deployment or production release; validate deterministic portable Linux/Windows suite and preserve previous CLI semantics.

structure: src/sf/deployment.py: synthetic coordinator, durable-log snapshot model and fake target authority / dispatch / recovery protocol
src/sf/cli.py: offline sf deployment qualify command only
tests/test_deployment.py: failure injection, state and event assertions against independent expectations
docs/factory/SF15_DEPLOYMENT_RECOVERY.md: precise authorization/unknown-outcome contract and simulation limits
impact: Adds isolated non-production qualification surface without enabling deployment to any real target
Provides reusable accepted source and operations handoff for future SF-16 and SF-19 acceptance campaigns

budget.network: No runtime network or third-party calls; GitHub provider API for PR evidence only
budget.execution: Local deterministic fixture tests first, then one stable exact-head Linux/Windows required CI run; no redundant runs

externalEffects: Only spsoftwarefc/s-f may be changed; do not operate on CTJ, Accordquill, VPS or cloud providers
Stack PR #26 on PR #25, keep #23–#27 unmerged, and reserve the next main integration for PR #28
No merge/release/deploy authority is granted by an SF-15 qualification result
